bullets.title: NVDA: Blowout quarter, 2nd largest single-day gain in US history; rev-share program intact
bullets.body: Nvidia posted its second-largest single-day gain in US stock market history on blowout results and guidance. The company denied pausing its revenue-sharing financing program, stating it 'continues to evolve due to strong demand'—analysts note 10%+ FY29 EPS upside if program expands per Nowak's cost assumptions. Funda raised FY28 revenue forecast to 68% growth; NVDA $230 calls were flagged as a key positioning tell. Implied vol collapsed ~32 points overnight. Citi published 'From Defense to Offense' coverage note separately.

bullets.title: MRVL: Down 7-8% AH despite solid beat; Oct 6 investor day the next catalyst
bullets.body: Marvell reported F2Q revenue $2.74bn (+37% YoY) and EPS $0.94 (slight beat), with F3Q guidance of $3.15bn (+50% YoY) and FY27E raised to ~$12bn. Stock fell 7-8% on elevated expectations and 90bps sequential GM compression. Hedgeye and sell-side consensus suggest buying the dip into the Oct 6 investor day, where expanded Google relationship and new CFO messaging on CY27 data center acceleration (60% growth, ~10% EPS upside) are expected catalysts.

bullets.title: AFRM: +11-12% on GAAP profitability inflection; FY27 GMV >$64B
bullets.body: Affirm Q4 revenue $1.17bn beat consensus $1.11bn; GAAP operating margin 12.6%, up 600bps YoY. Card penetration hit 19% of consumers, +124% YoY. Q1 guidance $1.19-1.22bn tops $1.16bn estimate; FY27 GMV guided >$64bn. Morgan Stanley TMT desk flagged as a key positive earnings surprise.

bullets.title: AVGO: Buy into Sep 3 earnings; CEO expected to calm GOOG share-loss fears
bullets.body: Broadcom has not had back-to-back down quarterly results in 7 years despite being down mid-teens recently. Hock Tan is expected to calm market fears about Google share losses and deliver bullish AI custom ASIC growth guides. MS hosting earnings callback with Joe Moore on Sept 3. Multiple desks flagging as a buy into the print.

bullets.title: TTWO: Bullish into Nov 19 GTA VI launch; $280-300 PT, 45M unit base case
bullets.body: Take-Two's 26-min GTA VI extended gameplay trailer on Netflix/YouTube received broadly positive reception. MS TMT desk models +13% average stock appreciation in final 3 months before major game launches; base case 45M units / $1.9B bookings, with GTA V-like penetration suggesting ~70% upside. Current PT range $280-300 vs stock at ~$235. Online/subscription monetization and in-game spend not yet in estimates.

bullets.title: CRM: Options volume 256% above average after 23% post-earnings rip on Anthropic deal
bullets.body: Salesforce options volume hit 214,675 contracts (256% above 30-day avg) with call-heavy positioning (P/C 0.61). Stock ripped ~23% as bears who were heavily short got squeezed; Cramer noted earnings upended bearish thesis. Rotation into software broadly sustained with the largest software net-buying day in one year yesterday.

bullets.title: DELL: F2Q preview soft; AI server raise to ~$75bn likely priced in
bullets.body: DELL F2Q27 estimates at $42.2bn revenue, below $44.5bn guidance midpoint, with gross margin 18.3% and EPS $4.70 vs consensus $4.84. NVIDIA L72 shipments cut to 17k units. While AI server guidance expected to raise to ~$75bn, desk notes the full-year AI server lift is likely already priced in. Stock down 1.3% pre-market.

bullets.title: MDB: Earnings tonight; 20-for-20 beat streak, ~15.7% implied move
bullets.body: MongoDB Q2 consensus is $735M revenue (above $729-734M guidance) and EPS $1.62 (above $1.58-1.61 guidance), with a 20-quarter perfect beat streak. Stock up 35.3% since May 28 vs S&P +2.2%. Options imply ~15.7% move; last four quarter moves: +3%, -22%, +22%, +38%. Q3 guide consensus at $745M revenue.

bullets.title: Software: Largest net-buying day in 1yr; most under-owned group near 2020 lows
bullets.body: Yesterday was the largest net buying day in Software in the last year with SaaS seeing 8 straight days of net buying. Gross/net exposure remains near 2020 lows, suggesting the squeeze has room to run. IGV returned -2.2% YTD vs S&P +12.9%; 'expensive' software up 39% in 3 months. CRWD and OKTA viewed as de-risked; rotation from semis/memory into software accelerating.

bullets.title: PYPL: Down 14-17% pre-market after Advent-Stripe $50B acquisition collapses
bullets.body: Advent and Stripe abandoned their $50 billion takeover bid for PayPal. PYPL options volume surged 263% above the 30-day average (161,962 contracts) with mixed sentiment (P/C 0.52). Stock was down 14-17% in pre-market trading.

bullets.title: IREN: Down 5.7% pre-market; $4bn contracted ARR, GPU financing at 9.0% fixed
bullets.body: IREN reported FY Q4 results that missed expectations but MS sales desk notes $4bn contracted ARR as of latest update and $2.8bn GPU financings at 9.0% fixed for $2.4bn. A multi-year Frontier AI Lab contract (separate from July announcement) was clarified. Jefferies roundtable on HPC/datacenter conversions featuring IREN on Sept 16 in NYC.

bullets.title: HUT: Down 3.1% in Canada pre-market; participating in Jefferies Real Estate and HPC roundtables
bullets.body: Hut 8 down 3.1% on TSX and 1.9% in US pre-market, tracking broader crypto/mining weakness. Jefferies hosting HPC/datacenter roundtable featuring HUT on Sept 16, highlighting its transition from Bitcoin mining to AI/HPC/cloud infrastructure. HUT also participating in Jefferies Annual Real Estate Conference Dec 7-8.

bullets.title: FCX: 22V flags 12.5-year base breakout vs S&P 500; 'must-own' technical setup
bullets.body: 22V Research Technical Team sees Freeport-McMoRan completing a 12.5-year base relative to the S&P 500 and expects an imminent breakout, calling it a 'must-own' after completion. FCX is already up 53% YTD. Separate UBS call advocates positioning for a broader commodity upcycle on global scarcity.

bullets.title: AAPL: Mac prices up 21-50%; foldable iPhone irrelevant to 75% of US adults
bullets.body: Apple raised Mac Studio prices 25-37% and Mac Mini 21-50%, despite expectations for anemic ex-iPhone hardware revenue growth—implying demand/unit erosion. A survey found 75% of US adults indifferent to a foldable iPhone, and consumers are holding phones longer due to memory shortages limiting upgrade cycles.

bullets.title: SMCI/CSCO: Cisco-Super Micro launch full-stack enterprise AI go-to-market partnership
bullets.body: Cisco and Super Micro launched a joint go-to-market partnership for full-stack enterprise AI solutions, signaling deeper integration between networking and compute in enterprise AI buildouts. DLR developing 50MW Singapore data center capacity expected to command premium pricing in tight market.

bullets.title: Commerce Dept drafting rules to block Chinese cloud access to US AI chips
bullets.body: The Trump administration is developing narrower AI chip access rules targeting Chinese developers' remote access to US chips in overseas data centers, closing cloud-computing workarounds around existing hardware restrictions. Affects US hyperscalers (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL) and chip makers (NVDA, AMD, INTC) operating in relevant markets.

bullets.title: MRVL/NVDA: CXMT revenue surges 10x in H1 2026, claiming #4 global DRAM position
bullets.body: Chinese memory maker CXMT reported H1 2026 revenue of 150.3bn yuan (+873% YoY) and net income of 77.6bn yuan, claiming fourth-largest DRAM maker globally. This intensifies competitive pressure on Western memory names (MU, SNDK, WDC) and adds to the rotation-out-of-memory narrative.

bullets.title: AFRM/UBER: AI inference optimization drives cost efficiency; Visa AI harness cuts cybersecurity spend
bullets.body: Uber weekly AI requests up 9.4x since February while total AI spending remains stable via inference optimization. Visa built an AI harness making Anthropic cheaper and faster for cybersecurity use cases—signaling enterprise AI cost discipline over raw spend growth.

bullets.title: GEV: CFO Ken Parks retiring; Claire McDonough (ex-Rivian) to join as replacement
bullets.body: GE Vernova CFO Ken Parks is retiring, with Claire McDonough (former Rivian CFO) joining as his replacement. Parks transitions to Strategic Advisor role in Q1 2027 before full retirement in April 2027. Leadership transition flagged by MS energy desk.

bullets.title: GS Prime: Defensives heavily net sold; Comm Svcs, Financials, Discretionary bought
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Prime data shows US L/S net leverage fell to 47.6% (1st percentile one-year). Single stocks net sold with short sales outpacing long buys 3.3:1. All defensive sectors (Healthcare, Utilities, Staples) saw largest $ net selling since April 2025. Comm Svcs, Financials, Consumer Discretionary, and Materials were the most net bought.
